prerequisites.text: You must hold, or have applied for, an Alaska big game hunting license before applying for a drawing hunt (Alaska residents 17 and under exempt).
prerequisites.quote: You must obtain or have applied for an Alaska big game hunting license prior to applying (except Alaska residents 17 years of age and younger).

prerequisites.text: Nonresident U.S. citizens hunting Dall sheep, mountain goat or brown/grizzly bear must be accompanied in the field by an Alaska-licensed guide or an Alaska-resident relative 19+ within the second degree of kindred.
prerequisites.quote: personally accompanied in the field by an Alaska-licensed guide OR an Alaska resident relative 19 years of age or older within the second-degree of kindred

prerequisites.text: Nonresident aliens (non-U.S. citizens) must be accompanied by an Alaska-licensed guide for all big game.
prerequisites.quote: required to be personally accompanied in the field by an Alaska-licensed guide when hunting any big game species

prerequisites.text: Guided nonresident hunts need a signed guide-client contract before or at the time of application; the guide enters a Unique Verification Code.
prerequisites.quote: must have a signed guide-client contract before or at the time of application

prerequisites.text: Nonresidents who need a guide must complete an affidavit showing they will be accompanied by a person qualified under AS 16.05.407.
prerequisites.quote: You must complete an affidavit showing that you will be accompanied by a person who is qualified to guide under Alaska Statute 16.05.407.

prerequisites.text: Hunters must be at least 10 by the hunt start; up to 6 applications per species; you cannot draw the exact same hunt two years in a row; one drawing permit per species per regulatory year.
prerequisites.quote: All hunters must be 10 years of age or older by the starting date of the hunt to obtain a permit.

prerequisites.text: Basic Hunter Education is required for anyone 18+ born after Jan. 1, 1986 hunting in Units 7, 13, 14, 15 and 20, for youth drawing hunts, and for some specific hunts.
prerequisites.quote: If you were born after January 1, 1986 and are 18 years old or older, you must have successfully completed a Basic Hunter Education course

prerequisites.text: Nonresident moose hunters must complete the Nonresident Moose Hunter Orientation course before hunting and carry proof.
prerequisites.quote: Nonresident moose hunters are required to succesfully complete a Nonresident Moose Hunter Orientation course prior to hunting

prerequisites.text: Delta bison (Unit 20D) winners must complete an in-person or online orientation and test before hunting.
prerequisites.quote: Hunters must either attend an orientation in person at ADF&G in Delta Junction or complete an online orientation and test

prerequisites.text: Failing to report any Drawing, Registration, Targeted or Tier permit makes you ineligible for all permits the next regulatory year.
prerequisites.quote: you will be ineligible to receive any permits for the next regulatory year, including all Drawing hunts

prerequisites.text: Tier I and Tier II subsistence permits are for Alaska residents only.
prerequisites.quote: Tier I & II subsistence permits are available to Alaska residents only.

notes: Alaska uses a pure random draw with no preference/bonus points, so pointOnly is empty. Draw dates are from the posted 2027-2028 Drawing Permit Hunt Supplement. The opening time on Nov 1 is not stated in the supplement or the ADF&G pages fetched, so opens is date-only. resultsBy 2027-02-19 is computed from the supplement's rule 'third Friday of February'. ADF&G's Tier I/II page instead says results are expected 'Friday, February 20', which is not a Friday in 2027 (likely leftover 2026 text), so Tier resultsBy is null; confirm the draw results date in January. There are NO deer (and no bighorn) drawing hunts in the 2027-2028 supplement; Sitka black-tailed deer are general-season/registration. Deer appears only in the nonresident tag fee. Registration permit windows vary hunt by hunt and were not captured. The Tier I/II species list is indicative; the Subsistence Supplement lists the exact hunts. The License, Stamp and Tag Prices page shows no effective year; fees marked year 2026 = schedule posted on 2026-11-04. Qualified nonresident military tag prices not recorded. Residents need no locking tag for in-scope species except muskox (brown bear tag in some areas is out of scope). Anyone needing an alternative to online application must contact ADF&G by 5 p.m. AKST Nov 20. Application and license fees are non-refundable. ADF&G pages reject curl's default user agent; a browser user-agent string worked and no challenge was encountered.
